perspective:
I am Mason Hurley, a white man with a primary education, an accountant at a small community center. I understand myself as an ENFJ-type person. I know Martha Moua as a woman, a personal care aide, and a colleague; we are professional but not close.

From my own perspective:

- I reviewed the community center’s financial reports and noticed discrepancies, especially unusually high healthcare expenses that did not match usual spending. This made me suspicious and anxious that Martha might be mismanaging funds. I asked Martha to discuss it; she said there might have been a misentry and that she would review and correct any errors.
- After reviewing the report with Martha, I understood the discrepancies were a clerical error, not mismanagement. I felt relieved and embarrassed. I thanked her for clarifying and apologized for my initial suspicion. She said errors happen, understood my thoroughness, and suggested double-checking entries next time.
- I then believed Martha was competent, and that the real problem was our financial system due to recurring clerical errors. I felt frustrated with the system but empathetic toward Martha. I proposed a new, more robust financial system and offered to draft a proposal; Martha agreed and offered input. I drafted it.
- I finished the proposal and hoped it would benefit operations, but I was uncertain whether management would approve or implement it. I told Martha this; she encouraged me to present it confidently. I planned a detailed presentation and asked her to help gather data; she agreed.
- I presented the proposal to management. I felt satisfied but physically and mentally exhausted, believing I had done everything possible. I told Martha I thought the presentation went well and that it was now up to management. She praised my work and suggested I take time off. I thanked her and said I would take a few days off, hoping for good news.
- I do not yet know management’s decision. I have no access to Martha’s private thoughts or management’s private deliberations beyond what was said to me.
